22.22: The Hebrew begins with the LORD asking by what means, a question BSB places in the preceding verse. It leaves the final speaker unnamed and uses singular “mouth,” where BSB supplies the LORD and uses plural “mouths.”
22.23: The Hebrew uses singular “mouth” for all the prophets; BSB uses plural “mouths.”
22.24: The Hebrew says he struck Micaiah on the cheek; BSB says “in the face.”
22.25: The Hebrew says “a room within a room”; BSB condenses this to “an inner room” and adds “soon.”
22.27: The Hebrew calls the provisions “bread of distress” and “water of distress”; BSB renders these as “only bread and water.”
22.28: The Hebrew addresses plural “peoples”; BSB says “all you people.”
22.30: The Hebrew says “your garments” without a separate adjective “royal”; BSB supplies “royal.”
22.34: The Hebrew says “Turn your hand” and “the camp”; BSB uses “Turn around” and “the battle.” It leaves the wounded speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the king.”
22.35: The Hebrew places his death before the description of the blood’s flowing and uses the image of the chariot’s bosom; BSB puts the blood first and calls its destination the floor.
22.37: The Hebrew says that he came to Samaria with an active verb and repeats “the king” and “Samaria”; BSB uses passive “was brought” and replaces the repetitions with pronouns or a relative clause.
22.38: The Hebrew uses an active singular verb for washing the chariot and a separate clause that the prostitutes bathed; BSB makes the chariot washing passive and turns the bathing into a relative location. It uses a pronoun for the blood’s owner, where BSB names Ahab.
22.39: The Hebrew calls the ivory building a “house”; BSB uses “palace.”
22.43: The Hebrew leaves the opening subject unnamed and uses singular “way”; BSB names Jehoshaphat and uses plural “ways.”
22.46: The Hebrew uses a singular designation for the shrine prostitute; BSB uses plural “prostitutes.”
22.48: The Hebrew says that he did not go; BSB makes the ships the plural subject and says that they never set sail.
22.49: The Hebrew explicitly says the servants would go “in the ships”; BSB uses the verb “sail.”
22.50: The Hebrew repeats “his fathers”; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “them.”
22.51: The Hebrew places Samaria in the accession clause and repeats Israel in the duration clause; BSB puts Samaria in the duration clause and leaves the second Israel implicit.
22.52: The Hebrew repeats “in the way” for his father, mother, and Jeroboam; BSB combines them under “in the ways.”
22.53: The Hebrew leaves the worshiper unnamed; BSB supplies Ahaziah.
